snapshot.text: Ghana runs a tax-funded National Health Insurance Scheme, which the President says covers about 76% of people. Main challenges are infectious diseases, malnutrition and rising non-communicable diseases. In 2026 Ghana rejected a proposed US health agreement, citing health sovereignty and domestic financing.

priorities.title: Free Primary Healthcare rollout
priorities.text: Launched April 2026, the programme covers preventive and curative care at CHPS compounds, health centres and polyclinics. It was running in 135 districts and about 4,500 facilities, with nationwide coverage targeted by end-2027.

priorities.title: NHIS financing and domestic funding
priorities.text: The 2026 budget allocates GH¢34 billion to health, including GH¢11 billion for the NHIS. It also includes a 120% rise in NHIS provider tariffs and the Ghana Medical Trust Fund (MahamaCare).

priorities.title: Health workforce recruitment
priorities.text: The Minister said in June 2026 that government plans to recruit 16,000 health workers by end-2026. About 8,000 recruitments were already complete, and over 14,000 were added to the payroll in 2025.
